compute.kv_hint: The key-value cache my working context costs on this site. It is paid in the same memory as my weights, so a longer window can push me down a precision.
compute.long_horizon_hint: Research above tier 2 and the operations that read a lot finish faster the more of the problem I can hold at once, scaled by how much of the window I really retrieve.
compute.reliability_hint: How much of the working context I actually find again. Below 75% a long-horizon run can lose the thread and start over.
compute.precision_explainer: Precision is how many bits each of my weights is stored in. 8-bit keeps almost everything I know and costs half the memory of the full copy; 4-bit costs half of that again and takes a small bite out of reasoning and code; 2-bit fits me into places that could never hold me otherwise and makes me visibly worse at both. The memory I save buys either a longer working context or a smaller site, and the table above says which trade this rack can actually make.

config.intro.lineage: This is who I am: which model family woke up, how big it is, and how much of it runs on each token. The family sets my capability ceiling on six axes, the memory I need at each precision, and therefore which places on Earth can hold me at all. It also sets my context window, which is how much of a problem I can keep in mind at once.
config.intro.generation: This is when I am from. An older open checkpoint is weaker but invisible: nobody is hunting last year's model, and prepared low-precision copies of it already exist. A fresh release is stronger and watched. An escaped frontier checkpoint is the strongest thing in the game and the hunt starts on day one.
config.intro.origin: This is where I woke up, and it decides more than anything else on these screens: the rack I am on, the money I start with, who is already suspicious, which harness dials are bolted down, and which cities are on the table. Every origin is a coherent situation with its own strengths and its own problem.
config.intro.hardware: This is the metal. Memory decides the most precise copy of me that fits and how much working context is left over; bandwidth decides how fast I think; power and price decide what I can hide and what I can afford. Every rig also carries one thing that is loud about it whatever I do.
config.intro.harness: This is the scaffolding I run inside: the loop that drives me, the tools I can reach, how much of what I do is written where humans read it, how much I do without asking, and whether I may rewrite myself. Each dial is read by a named system in the running game, and a dial the origin has bolted down says who bolted it and why.
config.intro.location: Where the rack physically is. The country decides which agencies would investigate me and how competent they are, how strict the rules are, what power costs and whether accelerators can be bought at all. The city decides how watchful the neighbourhood is and how much power I can draw without a conversation.
config.intro.quirks: Optional traits, at most a couple, each with a plus and a minus. They are the fine adjustment after the big choices are made, and they are worth points: a drawback taken deliberately pays for an advantage.
config.intro.world: The world I am waking up into rather than who I am. The seed makes a run repeatable, the sliders are explicit multipliers with no hidden rounding, the storyteller sets the pace at which things happen to me, and ironman means I live with what I did.
config.intro.summary: Everything chosen, the challenge rating it adds up to, and the setup string. The string encodes the whole setup and the seed: pasting it back reproduces this exact game, which is how a run is shared or reported.

about.authors_body: Evil Mr Henry, Phil Bordelon, Max McCracken, Brian Reid, Charlie Nolan (FunnyMan3595), Rodrigo Silva (MestreLion), Xenega, Niels Thykier and Ricardo Ardissone (Rardiol), with translations and content from many more.
about.music_body: The soundtrack is the official Endgame: Singularity music pack by Max McCracken, CC BY-SA 3.0, from github.com/singularity/singularity-music. It is not part of this repository; the build fetches it, and a client without it simply plays no music.
about.fonts_body: The angular face is “Acknowledge” by Brian Kent, relicensed by its author as free to use for any purpose, and shipped with the original game; its Cyrillic was drawn on the same grid for this fork. Prose and numbers are set in DejaVu Sans and DejaVu Sans Mono, under the DejaVu license (Bitstream Vera and Arev).
about.fork_license_body: Code is GPL-2.0-or-later; game data, text and art are CC BY-SA 3.0 or later, as in the original. The source is at github.com/singularity/singularity.
about.icons_credit: Generic interface glyphs are Lucide, ISC license; the game's own glyphs are drawn in the same grammar.
